author: mia
title: Credit card ban: what changed for online betting accounts
dek: Online wagering providers can no longer accept credit cards or digital currency. Here is what that means at deposit time.
body:
Online wagering providers in Australia can no longer accept credit cards or digital currency for deposits. The ban took effect on 11 June 2024 and applies to every licensed online and phone bookmaker. More than two years on, it still causes confusion at the deposit screen, so here is what changed and what it means in practice.

What the ban covers

The rule prevents wagering providers from accepting payment by credit card, either directly or through a third party that draws on a credit card. Digital currencies such as Bitcoin are banned for deposits as well. The aim is simple: people should not bet with borrowed money.

  • Credit cards, including those registered in digital wallets.
  • Payment services that are funded by a credit card in the background.
  • Cryptocurrency and other digital currencies.

Providers that break the rule face significant penalties, and licensed bookmakers have removed credit options from their apps and websites.

What still works

Most punters simply switched methods. The common options are:

MethodTypical speedNotes
Debit cardInstantVisa Debit and Mastercard Debit are accepted
PayIDUsually within minutesPaid from your bank app to an email or phone ID
BPAYOne to two business daysSlower, but useful for planned deposits
Bank transferSame day to two daysDepends on your bank

Some digital wallets still work, but only when they are linked to a debit card or bank account rather than a credit card.

Why a deposit might be declined

If your card is a credit card, the deposit will fail, even if it carries a Visa or Mastercard logo like a debit card. Some banks also issue cards that look similar for both products, so check the word "debit" on the card or in your banking app.

Debit cards linked to an overdraft can occasionally be declined too, because the provider cannot always tell where the funds come from. If that happens, PayID from a transaction account is usually the quickest alternative.

Withdrawals are not affected

The ban applies to deposits. Withdrawals still go back to your nominated bank account, and most licensed providers pay to PayID-enabled accounts within about an hour once the request is approved and your identity is verified.

The takeaway

Before your next deposit, check that the card in your account is a debit card or switch to PayID. While you are in the settings, it is a good moment to set or review a deposit limit, which every licensed provider must offer and which applies immediately when lowered.
